The outcome of a sensitivity analysis (S7)

Source: R/sensitivity.R
FlodeSensitivity.Rd

What rating_sensitivity() returns. It holds two tables:

  • results: one row per variant and stage, with test, variant (what was changed, in words), evidence_ids (a list column: the gaugings left out, empty for a test that leaves none out), stage_m, base_cms and variant_cms (discharge before and after), change_cms, change_pct, status and note;

  • summary: one row per variant, with the largest change in discharge and the stage it occurs at, and, for leave_one_out, the gauging's leverage and Cook's distance on the scale the fit minimised.

status is "ok", "not_converged" (the variant's own refit did not converge) or "refit_failed" (it could not be made, with the reason in note).

Usage

FlodeSensitivity(
  results = data.table(),
  summary = data.table(),
  stages = numeric(0),
  tests = character(0)
)

Arguments

results, summary

The two tables above.

stages

The stages the comparison was made at.

tests

The tests that were run.

Value

A FlodeSensitivity.

See also

rating_sensitivity(), sensitivity_summary(), sensitivity_results()

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage_m <- seq(0.4, 3, length.out = 16)
fit <- fit_rating(data.frame(stage_m = stage_m,
                             discharge_cms = 3.2 * stage_m^1.6 * exp(rnorm(16, sd = 0.04))), quiet = TRUE)
sens <- rating_sensitivity(fit, tests = "leave_high_out", stages = c(1, 2, 3))
class(sens)
#> [1] "reach.rate::FlodeSensitivity" "S7_object"                   
sensitivity_summary(sens)
#>              test                           variant        evidence_ids status
#>            <char>                            <char>              <list> <char>
#> 1: leave_high_out  without the highest 1 (top 6.2%)                G016     ok
#> 2: leave_high_out without the highest 2 (top 12.5%)           G016,G015     ok
#> 3: leave_high_out without the highest 4 (top 25.0%) G016,G015,G014,G013     ok
#>    max_abs_change_cms max_abs_change_pct stage_at_max_m leverage cooks_distance
#>                 <num>              <num>          <num>    <num>          <num>
#> 1:         0.02523195          0.1368095              3       NA             NA
#> 2:         0.36440412          1.9758261              3       NA             NA
#> 3:         0.59699813          3.2369681              3       NA             NA
#>      note
#>    <char>
#> 1:   <NA>
#> 2:   <NA>
#> 3:   <NA>
